scenes.headline: How a model manages its own context
scenes.sub: Context Language Models: the model edits its context file.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Vesper! Let me show you how a model can run its own memory, by treating its context as a file it rewrites.

scenes.text: Instead of a harness deciding what to forget, the model edits its context like a file: append, rewrite a line in place, or offload a chunk.
scenes.mark: edits its context like a file
scenes.label: The idea

steps.say: A turn starts with the live context.
It is mirrored as a plain text file the model can open.
The model reads the file and edits it with Bash. It can append, rewrite a line in place, or move a chunk out to storage.
The edit syncs back and becomes the context for the next turn.

left.title: Fixed harness
left.say: A fixed harness summarizes on a schedule. One lossy gist, and the exact fact you needed is gone.

right.title: The model
right.say: The model instead keeps the right lines and drops the rest, in any strategy it can write as code.

scenes.label: CLM accuracy on BrowseComp-Plus, zero-shot
scenes.note: 11.4% higher than the best harness, at 21.5% fewer FLOPs
scenes.say: With no training, this beats the strongest harness on a deep research benchmark, and gets there using less compute.

scenes.title: Learned in the weights
scenes.note: 47.6% better, 12% fewer FLOPs, on a nine billion model
scenes.say: Online reinforcement learning folds the strategy into the weights. A small model jumps a lot, and spends less compute doing it.

steps.say: An arbitrary edit is not free to serve. Standard serving re-prefills the whole tail after the edit, even text that never changed.
Suffix Cache Reuse keeps the unchanged tail's cache and splices it back, so only the edited part is recomputed.

scenes.text: Context management was the last piece of the agent loop written by hand. The model can learn to do it better.
scenes.mark: the model can learn to do it better

scenes.say: Context is a file. The model reads it, edits it, and keeps what matters. That's the whole idea. Thanks for watching!
